title: Lincoln’s definition of democracy
description: Abraham Lincoln provides a lasting standard for democracy, defining it as "government of the people, by the people and for the people".

title: Elections begin in Mexico
description: Mexico attains independence and begins holding presidential elections every six years, though one-party dominance would later challenge its democratic nature.

title: Universal adult franchise movements
description: The struggle for universal adult franchise links democracy to the demand that every adult citizen have one vote with one value.

title: Great Chinese famine
description: A massive famine in China kills three crore people; economists later argue this occurred because China lacked the accountability of a democratic government, free press, and opposition parties.

title: Independence of Zimbabwe
description: Zimbabwe attains independence from White minority rule.

title: Military coup in Pakistan
description: General Pervez Musharraf leads a military coup in Pakistan, overthrows a democratically elected government, and declares himself the ‘Chief Executive’.

title: End of PRI dominance in Mexico
description: The PRI (Institutional Revolutionary Party) in Mexico loses a Presidential election for the first time in 70 years, ending a long period of unfair electoral practices.

title: Legal Framework Order in Pakistan
description: In Pakistan, a ‘Legal Framework Order’ is issued to amend the constitution, giving the President power to dismiss national and provincial assemblies.

title: Elections in China
description: Elections are held in China for the National People’s Congress, though candidates still require approval from the Chinese Communist Party.

title: Women’s voting rights in Saudi Arabia
description: Saudi Arabia grants women the right to vote, following a long period where this right was denied.

title: Removal of Robert Mugabe
description: Robert Mugabe is forced out of office in Zimbabwe after decades of using unfair practices and increasing presidential power at the expense of accountability.
